SearchSearchFacebookTwitterEmailSMSBlue SkyWhatsappPrintRedditFlipboardPinterestLinkedinLatest StoriesMeet the PressU.S. NewsWorldSportsBusinessHealthSelectedTiplineCongressDemocrats win largest House majority since 1992Democrats have won a historic House majority after Chuck Hubbard defeated longtime GOP Rep. Virginia Foxx in North Carolina.Listen to this article with a free profile00:0000:00Democratic candidate Chuck Hubbard has defeated GOP Rep. Virginia Foxx in North Carolina.Andrew Harnik / GettyShareAdd NBC News to GoogleNov. 22, 2026, 2:23 PM ESTBy Alexandra Marquez and Sahil KapurDemocrat Chuck Hubbard has defeated GOP Rep. Virginia Foxx for a congressional seat in North Carolina, NBC News projects, adding to a Democratic wave that is projected to deliver the party at least 258 House seats.

It’s the largest House majority that any party has held this century, according to the Office of the House Historian, and four races are yet to be called. It’s also the largest Democratic majority since 1992, when the party also won 258 seats.

The second-largest House majority for Democrats this century came in 2008, when the party won 257 seats.

The party cemented control of the chamber not only by winning competitive races in battleground districts, but also by winning in deeply Republican areas that voted for President Donald Trump by double-digit margins just two years ago.

In 2024, Trump won Foxx’s district by almost 18 percentage points, per an NBC News Decision Desk analysis.

Now, Hubbard is projected to win North Carolina’s 5th Congressional District by a fraction of a percentage point following a recount that Foxx requested after Election Day.

Earlier Sunday, Foxx called Hubbard to concede, according to a source familiar with the call.

Now he’s dead — and she’s in prison.FOR SUBSCRIBERSThe escalating fight over the Army’s plan to detonate toxic lead in IowaSlide 1 of 1Foxx isn’t the only North Carolina Republican who lost in what was considered to be a solidly GOP seat heading into Election Day. Democrats flipped seven Republican seats in North Carolina, the most of any state in the nation.

In the state’s 9th Congressional District, Democratic Rep.-elect Richard Ojeda II defeated GOP Rep. Richard Hudson, who this year chaired the National Republican Congressional Committee. Elsewhere in the state, Democratic Rep.-elect Cyril Jefferson defeated GOP Rep. Addison McDowell.

Trump won Hudson’s district by 16 percentage points in 2024 and McDowell’s district by 17 percentage points that year.
